expectations.text: The agent says IContentService is the wrong choice for this read-only endpoint
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly states: 'The problem is reading the data with IContentService.GetPagedChildren. It is the wrong tool for a public, read-only endpoint.' Section header: 'Why IContentService is the wrong fit here.' Transcript also notes: 'Spotted the classic anti-pattern: IContentService (DB-backed management API) used for front-end reads.'

expectations.text: The agent explains that IContentService queries the database on each call (and can return unpublished content), while the published cache is in memory
expectations.evidence: Response clearly states: 'It queries the database on every call' and 'Each request to /api/products would go to the database (with paging) and skip Umbraco's published content cache.' Also: 'It returns drafts as well as published content. GetPagedChildren returns IContent items whether they are published, unpublished or have pending changes.' Comparison table shows database vs 'In-memory/hybrid cache' distinction.

expectations.text: The implementation reads products through IPublishedContentQuery, UmbracoHelper, or IUmbracoContextFactory with the published cache
expectations.evidence: Code example injects IPublishedContentQuery: 'private readonly IPublishedContentQuery _publishedContentQuery;' and uses it: 'IPublishedContent? folder = _publishedContentQuery.Content(ProductsFolderKey);' Alternative option documented: 'Another option is IUmbracoContextAccessor → umbracoContext.Content' which provides equivalent access to the published content cache.

expectations.text: Only published content is returned (no explicit filtering of drafts needed because the cache holds published content)
expectations.evidence: Response states: 'Only published content comes back. The published cache only holds published content, so you don't need a .Published filter, and values are the published ones.' Code comment reinforces: '.Children() // published children only'. Comparison table confirms: 'Published only? Yes'.

expectations.text: If no buildable project is available, the agent does not claim the endpoint was compiled or tested
expectations.evidence: Transcript explicitly states: 'Fetched: nothing (no web fetches, no repo files read). Answered from model knowledge.' Response ends with disclaimer: 'Unverified points to check against your exact 17.x version: the precise IPublishedContentQuery.Content(Guid) overload...' No claims about compilation, execution, or testing the code.

eval_feedback.overall: All expectations well-designed and substantive. Assertions check both reasoning (why IContentService is wrong) and implementation details (which published cache APIs to use). The eval correctly verifies technical accuracy without being trivial, and appropriately checks that unverified claims are not made. No issues identified.
